examples.en: The skin of the apple got scratched.
Don't judge people just by their outside.

examples.ko: 이 책은 거죽이 낡았지만 내용은 좋아요.
examples.en: This book's cover is worn, but the content is good.

examples.ko: 수박 거죽을 두드려 보면 익었는지 알아요.
examples.en: If you knock on the surface of a watermelon, you can tell if it's ripe.
The sofa covering tore, so I put on a new one.
The outside is fine, but the inside is all rotten.

explain: '겉'과 비슷하지만 속과 대비해서 겉모습이나 겉껍질을 말할 때 자주 써요. 반의어는 '속'이에요. '겉'보다 말투가 조금 거칠게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 과일은 겉이 깨끗해도 속이 상할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Fruit can be spoiled inside even if the outside looks clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거죽'보다 말투가 부드럽고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer in tone than 거죽 and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: The surface of the wall peeled off, so we repainted it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉껍질이나 겉면이 떨어질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for an outer layer or surface coming off.

phrases.example: 거죽과 속이 다른 사람은 믿기 어려워요.
phrases.en: It's hard to trust people whose outside and inside are different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반의어 '속'과 함께 써서 겉모습과 실제를 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with its opposite 속 to contrast appearance and reality.

explain_en: It is close to '겉' but is often used when contrasting the outside with the inside. Its opposite is '속'. It can sound a little rougher than '겉'.

examples.en: The security guard has a baton on his belt.
The rhythmic gymnast threw the clubs and caught them.
The club routine looks really difficult.
This club is made of plastic, so it is very light.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 곤봉으로 하는 체조를 배웠어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I learned gymnastics with clubs.

examples.ko: 경찰이 곤봉을 들고 입구 앞에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: A police officer was standing at the entrance holding a baton.

explain: 경비원이나 경찰이 쓰는 짧은 막대, 그리고 리듬체조 도구를 모두 곤봉이라고 해요. 일반적인 막대기는 '몽둥이'나 '방망이'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 경찰이 곤봉을 휘두르는 장면이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: A scene of police swinging batons was on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤봉을 크게 흔들 때 쓰는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing for swinging a club widely.

phrases.example: 경찰 곤봉은 보통 허리에 차고 있어요.
phrases.en: Police batons are usually worn at the waist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경찰이나 경비원이 쓰는 막대를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the stick used by police or guards.

phrases.example: 리듬체조 곤봉은 두 개를 같이 써요.
phrases.en: In rhythmic gymnastics, two clubs are used together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체조 도구를 말할 때 앞에 '리듬체조'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '리듬체조' in front when talking about the gymnastics equipment.

explain_en: '곤봉' covers both the short stick used by guards and police and the clubs used in rhythmic gymnastics. A plain stick is more often called '몽둥이' or '방망이'.

en: to be sick all the time

examples.en: My grandmother has been unwell all the time lately.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 골골해서 학교를 자주 빠졌어요.
examples.en: I was sickly as a child, so I often missed school.

examples.ko: 골골한 사람이 오래 산다는 말도 있어요.
examples.en: There is a saying that sickly people live long.
My body is weak, so I feel ill every time the seasons change.

examples.ko: 골골해 보이지만 사실은 건강 검진 결과가 좋아요.
examples.en: He looks frail, but actually his health checkup results are good.

examples.ko: 일이 많은 달에는 늘 골골하게 지내요.
examples.en: In busy months I always go around feeling under the weather.

explain: '아프다'와 달리 크게 아픈 건 아니지만 늘 기운이 없고 자주 앓는 상태에 써요. 반대말은 '튼튼하다'예요. 말투가 가벼워서 '골골거리다'와 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has been feeling sickly for several days because of a cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골골하다'와 뜻이 같지만 말투가 더 가벼워서 편한 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 골골하다 but sounds lighter, so it suits casual conversation.

phrases.example: 저는 몸이 약해서 늘 골골한 편이에요.
phrases.en: I'm physically weak, so I tend to be sickly all the time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편이다'를 붙이면 자주 아픈 편이라고 부드럽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '편이다' softly says that you tend to be sickly.

phrases.en: These days I exercise, so I'm not sickly anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 예전과 달리 자주 아프지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says you no longer get sick often.

explain_en: Unlike '아프다', it means not seriously ill but constantly low on energy and often unwell. Its opposite is '튼튼하다'. The tone is light, and it is used much like '골골거리다'.

en: to be rather bent; to be rather arched

examples.en: My grandfather's back is a little bent, but he walks fast.
After sitting for a long time, my shoulders got hunched.
If you study with a hunched posture, your neck hurts.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 키가 큰데 늘 구부정하게 서 있어요.
examples.en: He is tall, but he always stands with a stoop.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 등이 구부정하다고 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend told me my back is a bit hunched.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 몸이 구부정해지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think the body gets more bent as people age.

explain: 허리나 등처럼 사람 몸이 조금 굽은 모습에 주로 써요. 반대는 '꼿꼿하다'예요. 물건이 휜 모양은 보통 '구부러지다', '휘다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: A slouched posture is bad for your health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허리나 등이 조금 굽은 자세를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a posture with a slightly bent back.

phrases.en: Don't sit hunched; straighten your back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구부정하게'는 동사 앞에 쓰는 부사 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, used before a verb.

phrases.en: That person's shoulders look a bit hunched.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it looks that way from the outside.

explain_en: It is mostly used for a person's body, such as a back or waist that is slightly bent. The opposite is '꼿꼿하다' (upright). For bent objects, people usually say '구부러지다' or '휘다'.

examples.ko: 편지를 읽던 할머니가 눈시울을 붉히며 흐느끼셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma, reading the letter, sobbed with reddened eyes.
Listening to the song, my eyes grew warm with tears.
My friends' eyes got moist at the graduation.
My father's eyes turned slightly red.
My eyes sting with emotion at the touching story.

examples.ko: 눈시울이 젖은 채로 그는 웃어 보였어요.
examples.en: He smiled with his eyes still moist.

explain: 눈 가장자리를 뜻하지만, 거의 감동하거나 슬플 때 눈물이 날 것 같은 모습에만 써요. '눈시울이 붉어지다/뜨거워지다/젖다'가 자주 붙는 말이에요. 단순히 눈 모양을 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 그는 옛 친구를 만나고 눈시울을 붉혔어요.
phrases.en: He teared up when he met his old friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈물이 날 만큼 감동하거나 슬퍼한다는 뜻이고, 눈물이 흐르기 전의 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means being moved or sad enough to get teary, typically before tears actually fall.

explain_en: It means the rim of the eye, but it is used almost only for moments of being moved or sad when tears are about to come. It commonly pairs with '붉어지다/뜨거워지다/젖다'. You don't use it to describe eye shape.

examples.en: I got hit in the stomach and the pit of my stomach really hurts.
I ate too fast, and the area around my solar plexus feels stuffy.
Please don't press hard on the pit of my stomach.
When I'm nervous, the bottom of my breastbone throbs and stings.

examples.ko: 의사가 명치 부분을 살짝 눌러 봤어요.
examples.en: The doctor gently pressed on the area of my solar plexus.
Maybe it's indigestion; it feels like something is stuck in the pit of my stomach.

explain: 가슴뼈 아래, 배 윗부분 가운데를 가리켜요. 체했을 때나 맞았을 때 '배'라고 하기보다 '명치가 아프다'고 정확히 말해요. '명치끝'이라고도 하고, 병원에서도 이 위치를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: My upper stomach hurts; maybe I have indigestion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아픈 위치를 정확히 말할 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to name the exact spot that hurts.
phrases.en_equiv: to have pain in the pit of the stomach

phrases.en: I got hit in the solar plexus by the ball and couldn't breathe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동이나 싸움에서 그 부위를 세게 맞았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when that spot is hit hard in sports or a fight.
phrases.en_equiv: to be hit in the solar plexus

phrases.en: The tip of my solar plexus feels tight and sore.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명치'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 가슴뼈 아래 끝부분을 조금 더 정확히 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, but points a bit more precisely to the lower tip of the breastbone.
phrases.en_equiv: the very pit of the stomach

explain_en: It points to the middle of the upper abdomen, just below the breastbone. When you have indigestion or got hit, people say '명치가 아프다' to be precise instead of just '배'. It is also said as '명치끝', and used at hospitals to describe this spot.

examples.en: The baby squirms in the bed, refusing to sleep.
He struggled with all his might to escape poverty.

examples.ko: 잠을 잘 때 몸부림치는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of thrashing around when I sleep.
No matter how much I struggled, the situation didn't improve.
After struggling desperately to survive, he finally succeeded.

examples.ko: 몸부림치며 울던 아이를 엄마가 안아 줬어요.
examples.en: The mother hugged the child who had been crying and thrashing.

explain: 아파서 또는 화가 나서 몸을 마구 비틀 때 쓰고, 힘든 상황에서 벗어나려고 애쓰는 모습에 비유로도 많이 써요. 명사 '몸부림'을 써서 '몸부림을 치다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The baby thrashes around while sleeping.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몸부림치다'를 '몸부림을 치다'로 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A split form of 몸부림치다.

phrases.en: I flailed in the water to survive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손발을 마구 움직이며 애쓰는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes frantically moving limbs while struggling.

phrases.example: 아이는 장난감을 사 달라고 몸부림치며 울었어요.
phrases.en: The child cried and writhed, asking for a toy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 다른 행동과 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -며, it links to another action.

explain_en: It can mean twisting your body wildly from pain or anger, and it is often used figuratively for struggling hard to escape a difficult situation. You can also use the noun and say '몸부림을 치다'.

examples.en: I worked all day, so my whole body aches.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날이면 할머니는 삭신 쑤신다고 하세요.
examples.en: On rainy days, Grandma says her whole body aches.

examples.ko: 이사를 마쳤더니 삭신에 힘이 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: After finishing the move, my whole body has no strength left.
With this cold, even my whole body hurts.
My body is fine, but my mind is worn out.
I massaged my mother's aching body.

explain: 거의 '삭신이 쑤시다'처럼 몸이 아프고 결릴 때 써요. 어른들, 특히 나이 드신 분들이 많이 쓰는 정겨운 말이고, 젊은 사람은 '온몸이'라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: My whole body aches after sitting for so long.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삭신이 쑤시다'보다 더 일반적으로 아프다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general way to say the body aches than 삭신이 쑤시다.

phrases.en: The weather's bad, so my whole body aches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸 여기저기가 욱신욱신 아프다는 느낌으로, 나이 드신 분들이 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Conveys a throbbing ache all over the body, and older people often say it.

phrases.en: I caught a cold, so my whole body hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젊은 사람들이 '삭신' 대신 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What younger people use more often instead of 삭신.

explain_en: It is used almost only in phrases like '삭신이 쑤시다' when your body aches. It is a familiar, warm word often used by older people, while younger people more often say '온몸이'.

en: inside one's hand; within one's grasp

examples.en: The little bird fit snugly into my hand.

examples.ko: 요즘은 스마트폰 하나로 손안에서 은행 일을 다 봐요.
examples.en: These days, I handle all my banking in the palm of my hand with a single smartphone.
The sand in my hand slipped away.

examples.ko: 손안에 땀이 나서 펜이 자꾸 미끄러졌어요.
examples.en: My palm was sweaty, so the pen kept slipping.

examples.ko: 아이는 사탕을 손안에 꼭 쥐고 있었어요.
examples.en: The child was holding the candy tightly in their hand.

examples.ko: 동전을 손안에 감추고 마술을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: He hid a coin in his hand and showed me a magic trick.

explain: '손바닥'은 손의 평평한 면이고, '손안'은 손을 오므렸을 때 그 안쪽 공간에 가까워요. 보통 '손안에', '손안의'처럼 조사와 함께 쓰고 붙여 써요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 몇 년 만에 시장을 손안에 넣었어요.
phrases.en: to take full control of something
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 쥐는 것이 아니라 어떤 힘이나 대상을 완전히 차지하고 마음대로 할 수 있게 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean holding an object but gaining complete control over some power or target.
phrases.en_equiv: have something in the palm of one's hand

explain_en: '손바닥' is the flat surface of the hand, while '손안' is closer to the space inside the hand when you close it. It is usually written as one word and used with particles, as in '손안에' or '손안의'.

en: to shut one's teeth; to set one's teeth

examples.en: I clenched my teeth to bear the pain.
He clamped his mouth shut and held back his tears.
I gritted my teeth and ran to the end.

examples.ko: 악다문 입으로 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: With a tightly shut mouth, he said nothing.
He seemed angry and clenched his jaw.

examples.ko: 이를 악다물며 무거운 짐을 들어 올렸어요.
examples.en: I lifted the heavy load with gritted teeth.

explain: 입이나 이를 힘껏 꽉 다물 때 써요. 힘든 것을 참거나 굳게 각오할 때, 또는 화가 날 때 나오는 모습이에요. '다물다'가 ㄹ받침이라 '악다문'처럼 ㄹ이 빠져요. 비슷한 '이를 악물다'도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I gritted my teeth to go all the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이를 악다물다'와 같은 뜻이고 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'ireul akdamulda' and used more often.

phrases.en: He clenched his mouth shut in anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 대신 입이 목적어가 되어 입을 꽉 닫는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'mouth' as the object, it describes clamping the mouth shut.

phrases.en: I could feel firm resolve in his tightly shut mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '악다물다'를 '악다문'으로 활용해서 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form 'akdamun', used to describe a noun.

explain_en: Use it when you press your mouth or teeth tightly shut with force, such as enduring pain, resolving firmly, or being angry. 다물다 is an ㄹ-stem verb, so the ㄹ drops in forms like '악다문'. The similar '이를 악물다' is also common.

examples.ko: 아이가 잔병치레가 잦아서 병원에 자주 가요.
examples.en: My child gets sick often, so we go to the hospital a lot.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 어릴 때 잔병치레를 많이 했어요.
examples.en: My son was sick a lot when he was little.

examples.ko: 잔병치레 한 번 안 하고 겨울을 보냈어요.
examples.en: I got through the winter without being sick even once.
I suffer from one minor illness after another every change of season.

examples.ko: 잔병치레는 커 가면서 점점 줄어들 거예요.
examples.en: The frequent sickness will gradually decrease as they grow.
Since I started exercising, I no longer get sick often.

explain: '잔병'이 가벼운 병 자체라면, '잔병치레'는 그런 병을 자주 앓는 일을 가리켜요. 주로 아이나 몸이 약한 사람에게 쓰고 '잔병치레를 하다'가 기본 모양이에요.

phrases.en: My daughter hardly ever gets sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 아프지 않고 튼튼하다는 뜻이에요. 아이 건강을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means one is sturdy and rarely falls ill; often used for children's health.

phrases.en: My younger sibling gets sick often every winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감기 같은 가벼운 병을 자주 앓는다는 뜻이에요. '잔병치레를 자주 하다'와 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting minor illnesses like colds often; same meaning as '잔병치레를 자주 하다'.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 잔병치레하던 아이가 지금은 튼튼해졌어요.
phrases.en: The child who used to be sickly is now strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잔병치레를 하다'를 한 동사처럼 줄인 말이에요. 어릴 때를 돌아볼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened verb form of '잔병치레를 하다', often used when looking back on childhood.

explain_en: While '잔병' is the minor illness itself, '잔병치레' is the experience of getting such illnesses over and over. It is mostly used for children or people with a weak body, and the basic pattern is '잔병치레를 하다'.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 감기 특효약은 없다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said there is no miracle cure for colds.
There is still no wonder drug for this illness.
They say laughter is a miracle cure for stress.
Grandmother's love is the best remedy for me.

examples.ko: 광고에서 특효약처럼 말하는 제품은 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You should be careful with products that are advertised like miracle cures.
That book felt like a cure for me.

explain: 약뿐 아니라 '웃음이 스트레스의 특효약이다'처럼 문제를 잘 풀어 주는 방법을 비유할 때도 많이 써요. '만병통치약'은 모든 병에 듣는 약이라는 더 큰 말이에요. 광고의 특효약 설명은 믿기 전에 확인해야 해요.

phrases.en: There is no cure-all in the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모든 병에 듣는다는 약을 말하고, '특효약'보다 범위가 훨씬 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: A medicine said to cure every illness; much broader in scope than 특효약.

phrases.en: People look for a miracle drug for losing weight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 쉽게 풀어 줄 방법을 찾을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when looking for an easy fix to a problem.

phrases.en: Exercise is a miracle cure for stress.
phrases.nuance_ko: '스트레스의 특효약'처럼 무엇을 잘 풀어 주는 방법을 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively, as in 'a cure for stress', for something that solves a problem well.

explain_en: Besides real medicine, it is often used figuratively for something that solves a problem well, as in '웃음이 스트레스의 특효약이다'. '만병통치약' is a bigger word meaning a cure for every illness. You should check claims of a miracle cure in ads before believing them.

examples.ko: 밤에 아무도 없는데 누가 부르는 환청이 들렸어요.
examples.en: At night, with nobody there, I heard what sounded like someone calling me.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 환청까지 들리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm so tired that I feel like I'm even hearing things.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 진동 환청 때문에 자꾸 확인해요.
examples.en: I keep checking because I imagine my phone vibrating.

examples.ko: 그 소리는 환청이 아니라 진짜 옆집 소리였어요.
examples.en: That sound wasn't in my head; it was really the neighbor's noise.

examples.ko: 환청이 계속되면 병원에 가 보는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If you keep hearing things, it's good to see a doctor.

examples.ko: 환청 증상이 있는 사람은 전문가의 도움이 필요해요.
examples.en: People with symptoms of auditory hallucinations need professional help.

explain: 실제로 나지 않는 소리가 들리는 것을 말하고, 보통 '환청이 들리다'라고 써요. 일상에서는 피곤할 때 소리를 잘못 들은 느낌을 가볍게 말할 때도 있어요. 눈에 보이는 가짜 모습은 '환각'이나 '환영'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm so tired that I hear things that aren't there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 나지 않는 소리가 들린다고 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrasing for hearing sounds that aren't really there.
phrases.en_equiv: to hear things that aren't there

phrases.en: He said he hears voices that aren't there every night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used when the listener is the subject.

phrases.example: 약 때문에 환각이 나타날 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Hallucinations can appear because of medication.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리뿐 아니라 눈에 보이는 가짜 모습까지 넓게 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that covers false sights as well as sounds.

explain_en: It is the experience of hearing sounds that are not really there, usually said as '환청이 들리다'. In daily life people also use it lightly when they think they heard something because they are tired. Seeing things that aren't there is '환각' or '환영'.
